s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pelvic pain with abdominal mass and recent aggravation
salient_findings: Persistent right lower abdominal pain for eight years
10 cm palpable mass in pelvic cavity fixed to anterior rectum
Hard texture and significant tenderness of the mass
key_facts: 40-year-old woman with history of multiple surgeries
Pain in the right lower abdomen persisting for eight years
Recent aggravation of pain and abdominal expansion sensation
Soft and tender abdomen in the lower part without rebound tenderness
10 cm mass palpable in pelvic cavity with clear boundary and hard texture
Mass fixed to anterior rectum with significant tenderness and limited mobility
Smooth mucosa on rectal examination with a hard, mobile, non-tender mass
CA125 level of 35.08 U/ml
LH level of 44.87 IU/L, FSH level of 108.8 IU/L
MRI and CT findings of irregular mass in pelvic area with multiple nodules
Biopsy results showing smooth muscle tumor
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD34, SMA, desmin, and others

shortlist.label: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Smooth muscle tumor on biopsy and history of multiple uterine surgeries

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD34 and SMA, and mass location near rectum

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Hard texture and limited mobility of the mass, and history of multiple surgeries

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large pelvic mass with clear boundary and hard texture, and history of multiple gynecological surgeries

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Smooth muscle tumor on biopsy and positive immunohistochemistry for CD34 and SMA

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a large, fixed, and tender mass in the pelvic cavity with a clear boundary and hard texture, along with the biopsy results showing a smooth muscle tumor and immunohistochemistry positive for CD34, SMA, desmin, and others, is consistent with aggressive angiomyxoma. The tumor's location, size, and fixation to the anterior rectum also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient has undergone a total abdominal hysterectomy, making a uterine origin of the tumor unlikely.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: The tumor's location and fixation to the anterior rectum, as well as the immunohistochemistry results, do not support a gastrointestinal origin.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: The tumor's size, location, and aggressiveness are not typical of desmoid tumors, which are usually smaller and less symptomatic.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: The tumor's morphology and immunohistochemistry results do not support a diagnosis of solitary fibrous tumor, which typically shows a more benign appearance and lacks the smooth muscle markers seen in this case.
